title: FOREIGN KEY Constraint
description: Learn how to use the FOREIGN KEY constraint to enforce referential integrity between tables.

data.text: A foreign key is a column or group of columns in one table that uniquely identifies a row in another table. The FOREIGN KEY constraint enforces a link between data in two tables, ensuring referential integrity.

data.title: FOREIGN KEY Syntax
data.content: Creates a foreign key constraint linking child and parent tables.
data.code:
CONSTRAINT fk_constraint_name
FOREIGN KEY (column_1, column2,...)
REFERENCES parent_table_name(column1,column2,..)

items: The constraint name is optional. If omitted, SQL Server generates a name automatically.
Specify the foreign key columns in parentheses after the FOREIGN KEY keyword.
Specify the parent table and the referenced columns after the REFERENCES keyword.

data.text: Consider vendor_groups and vendors tables where each vendor belongs to a vendor group.

data.title: Create Tables with FOREIGN KEY
data.content: Creates parent and child tables with a foreign key relationship.

data.text: The vendor_groups table is the parent table and the vendors table is the child table.
The foreign key constraint allows you to define referential actions when a row in the parent table is updated or deleted:

items: ON DELETE NO ACTION: Raises an error and rolls back the delete (default).
ON DELETE CASCADE: Deletes corresponding rows in the child table.
ON DELETE SET NULL: Sets child table rows to NULL (column must be nullable).
ON DELETE SET DEFAULT: Sets child table rows to their default values.
ON UPDATE actions work similarly for updates to the parent table.

data.title: FOREIGN KEY Key Points
points: FOREIGN KEY enforces referential integrity between tables.
The child table references the parent table via the foreign key column.
Referential actions (CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT) control cascading behavior.
By default, ON DELETE NO ACTION prevents deletion of referenced parent rows.
You can define foreign keys inline or as table constraints.
